content.text: All four subsections align with the preferred position, and nothing elsewhere undercuts them.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets our preferred position in full. 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or to an M&A successor (notice only). 24.2 bars Vendor from assigning, delegating material performance, or transferring by change of control without our consent (reasonableness standard) and never to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control, and requires cooperation with successor administrative changes. 24.3 does not undercut 24.1 because it is expressly limited to "other assignments" (i.e., those outside the 24.1 carve-out) and applies mutually with a not-unreasonably-withheld standard. Section 13.3 tracks Section 24 by letting Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a permitted assignment. A document-wide search for "change of control" and "assign" surfaced no deemed-assignment trigger or Vendor exit/re-pricing right; 9.2's insolvency clause is mutual and expressly excludes lawful reorganizations that do not impair performance. No redline needed.
